title: Village Quest
text: “Wolf, Keel-kun, can’t Ren track them by scent?”
“Stop treating me like a dog!”
Ren was protesting here too, but inult tracking abilities were quite high, I say.
“I tried following the smell, but it cut off partway through and I couldn’t figure it out.”
“Indeed, Naofumi-sama. Partway through, the scent vanishes as though the culprit flew through the air or bounded across treetops. Could it be that some monster of that sort carried them off…”
Keel and Wolf seemed to be sniffing around, each trying to track the scent in their own way.
“Theo can’t tell from sound either?”
“Even so…”

Rabbit Guy was in his rabbit form trying to listen for surrounding sounds, but he didn’t seem to detect anything either. Incidentally, Crocodile Guy was searching a different area together with Éclair. Panda and Elephant, and Older Sister as well, were also searching, but unfortunately they’d split off separately.
“How about you Filolial-samas?”

Yuki-chan, Kou, and Luna-chan were present. Filo-tan was over at Panda’s village with Big Sister and the others, so she wasn’t here right now. Ah, Filo-tan… I really didn’t want to go searching in dragon territory, I say. Dragon territory was Destroy’s stomping grounds, after all.
“It’s so dragon-stinky it’s hard to judge, nano.”
“Stinkyyy.”
“Keel-kun and Ama can tell, but the rest of us have no idea~”

The tracking seemed to be proving quite difficult indeed. If we went too deep into the mountains, Rival’s parent might well show up… A poorly-handled clash would be troublesome enough, but worse, we might run into a Rival who hadn’t looped. Thinking such thoughts, the mountain search had turned into something resembling a full-on manhunt, splitting personnel further and further.
“By the way, what kind of kid was the one who got taken?”
Father asked Keel and Ren.
“Huh? Um… some kid who was just there before we knew it while we were all playing.”
“A demi-human.”
“Now that you mention it, I thought it was a village kid, but it was a demi-human kid.”
Father tilted his head at Keel and the others’ answers.
“There was a demi-human kid in that village? If it were a traveler’s or adventurer’s child, the parents would probably be making a fuss… but we came out here before confirming with the parents, so…”

Lazy Pig seemed to be over there taking a head count. Assistant suddenly floated up in the back of my mind, but surely it couldn’t be that a circus had come, a festival had been thrown, and she’d wandered on over to the bustling village out of idle curiosity—impossible, I say! Somewhere in my mind I felt like Rival was scowling and saying “Nano, say it if you know, nano!” but that daddy’s girl would never come out of mere curiosity like that.
And so, as we pushed on through the mountains parting the very roots of the grass… we’d finally gone far enough that we were bound to run into Rival’s parent sooner or later.
“GYAOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!”
With that roar, Rival’s parent appeared. Ngh… I really would have preferred not to meet it, I say.
“Everyone! Fall back!”
Rival’s parent breathed fire, and Father stepped forward to take the hit. In that opening, Ren tried to circle around to its flank, so I followed to keep an eye on him.
“Ren, you mustn’t kill it, I say.”
“You’re still saying that?! This dragon might be the very ringleader who abducted the child!”
If that turned out to be true, it would be trouble beyond measure indeed.
“As we are now, we should be able to take it alive. Like so!”
And with that, I skewered Rival’s parent with Paralyze Lance V.
“GYAAAA—GYAOOO—GYAAAOOOOO!”
Struck by my Paralyze Lance V, Rival’s parent reeled backward. Well, if I got serious, this was small fry I could kick around without effort. Even Ren, enhanced as he was, could take it down easily.
“Hmph!”
Shwip! Ren swung his sword and cleanly sliced Rival’s parent’s flank. Splurt! Blood gushed out.
“That’s a bit too deep a cut, I say. Are you trying to make it fatal?”
“Just a mistake.”
Ever since becoming an inult, Ren had gotten decently good at enhancement methods, so of course Rival’s parent was simple for him to bring down.
“If you keep attacking this recklessly, Ren, I’ll have to restrain you, I say.”
“Whose side are you even on?!”
“Me? I’m on Father’s side, and Filolial-sama’s side, I say!”
Ren existed only to keep the number of Rivals from increasing and as a pet for Luna-chan and Kuro-chan, nothing more.
“Regardless, that was too deep a cut, I say.”
I cast healing magic on it so we wouldn’t let Rival’s parent die.
“Here we goooo!”
“Yah!”
“Luna too!”
The Filolial-samas joined in as well, so I had to caution them. Truth be told, I too would have loved nothing more than to finish it off and celebrate a grand victory with everyone.
“Everyone, please go easy on it, I say!”
“Ehh…”
“That request is a hard one to grant, nano…”
“Booo.”
Of course, Yuki-chan and the other Filolial-samas, having heard my request, held back just enough while still thoroughly pummeling Rival’s parent.
“Gya! Gyaooo! Gyaaa—”

Even when it breathed fire, the attacks were dodged or deflected—no, Filolial-sama merely fanned her wings and the flames veered off course. It tried flapping its wings to flee into the sky, but those very wings got kicked by Filolial-sama and snapped, leaving it unable to fly properly. By this point, word of the commotion had spread, and Wolf, Rabbit Guy, and Crocodile Guy had all come running to watch the battle from a distance. Having heard that Rafumi and I preferred not to kill dragons, the flow of things had settled into simply not engaging further.
“Man… it’s like coming to hunt monsters ranked Dos, or G, or S in some hunting game, but instead wandering into a low-level quest by mistake—that’s the difference in power here.”
Father cast a sympathetic glance at Rival’s parent, who by now looked utterly pitiful after being pummeled so thoroughly.
“Big bro… dragons are supposed to be super scary creatures in stories, but getting beat up like that, it’s not scary at all anymore.”
Keel, not participating in the fight, offered her impression to Father.

“Well… it’s because an excess of manpower relative to the actual threat keeps swarming in here one after another… honestly, it’s gotten to the point where I can’t deny it feels less like fighting a dragon and more like we’re just bullying it for fun.”
“Woof, Naofumi-sama. Shall I finish it off?”
“Apparently we’re not allowed to.”

“Dragons are supposed to be full of romance in stories, but having been dragged along to witness these people hunting them down like this, it’s become nothing more to me than experience points… there’s no romance in it at all, is there.”
“How pitiful… I feel like it’d be kinder to just put it out of its misery.”
“Indeed… now that we’ve regrouped, has the child in question been found, Iwatani-dono?”
“Not yet. Since we’re the ones drawing the dragon’s attention, everyone else should prioritize the search.”
“So this is what it means for heroes to be this strong, I suppose… but there’s simply no sense of tension to it.”
Wolf, Rabbit Guy, Crocodile Guy, and Éclair each asked their questions while watching Rival’s parent’s pathetic state. And so it seemed Éclair and the others would prioritize the search after all.
“Oh, Naofumi-chan. Did you find the kid?”
“Nope. The dragon showed up instead, so we’re planning to weaken it and hold it down without killing it, so please prioritize the search.”
“Got it~”

Older Sister, along with Panda and Elephant, joined us as well but soon departed again. They’d judged the battle would be over shortly. As for what I was doing, I kept casting healing magic on the spots where the wound looked like it might turn fatal. Wearing down its stamina was the important part, after all.
“I don’t have time to deal with you right now, I say! Sleep or paralysis, which would you prefer, I say?”
“Wheeze… wheeze… gya, gya…”
To Rival’s parent, now on death’s door and barely breathing, I delivered my final ultimatum.
“Stop it!”

And just then… Assistant came dashing out together with what appeared to be Rival’s sibling monster, stepping in front of Rival’s parent to shield it, spreading her arms wide and standing her ground. Ngh… so she really did come out here. I have no business with you right now, I say.
“Don’t you dare bully Papa!”
